mission.title: Strong authentication and privileged access — Keycloak
mission.lead_auditor: Attest CI (automated run, no human auditor)
scope_in: Security settings of the Keycloak realm (password, lockout, session, logging)
Realm accounts and members of the admin role
scope_out: Intrinsic strength of MFA factors and custom authentication flows
Clients, identity federation and connected applications
Hosting and operation of the Keycloak server

target_label: Keycloak (open-source identity provider), through the read-only gateway

control.title: MFA enforced for privileged administrator accounts
control.objective: Every account holding the realm role admin has multi-factor authentication configured.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve all members of the realm role admin via paginated GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users and verify totp is true for each account.
control.expected: totp=true for every object from GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users
control.risk: Without MFA, a single stolen privileged password allows full takeover of the identity provider and all connected critical functions.
control.recommendation: Require OTP enrollment for all admin accounts and enforce MFA for the admin authentication flow.
control.cause: MFA was likely left optional in the realm authentication configuration or administrator onboarding process.

before.expected: totp=true for every object from GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users

control.title: MFA enforced for users of critical system
control.objective: Every user account in the realm, which supports critical or important functions, has multi-factor authentication configured.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve all users via paginated GET /api/kc/users and verify totp is true for each account.
control.expected: totp=true for every object from GET /api/kc/users
control.risk: Without MFA, password-only authentication exposes critical functions to account takeover by phishing or credential stuffing.
control.recommendation: Require OTP enrollment for all realm users and enforce MFA for the user authentication flow.
control.cause: MFA was likely not made mandatory in the realm authentication flow or user lifecycle process.

before.expected: totp=true for every object from GET /api/kc/users

control.title: Strong password policy with length and complexity
control.objective: The realm passwordPolicy requires minimum length of 12 characters with complexity requirements.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve GET /api/kc/realm and parse passwordPolicy to verify length and complexity items are present.
control.expected: passwordPolicy contains length(12) or greater and upperCase(1), lowerCase(1), digits(1) and specialChars(1)
control.risk: Weak passwords can be guessed or brute-forced, leading to unauthorized access to critical identity services.
control.recommendation: Set the realm password policy to enforce at least 12 characters with upper-case, lower-case, digit and special-character complexity.
control.cause: The realm password policy was likely left at Keycloak defaults and never hardened to the internal standard.

test.code:
import requests
import json
import os
import sys
import re
if "LAB_URL" not in os.environ:
    sys.stderr.write("missing LAB_URL\n")
    sys.exit(2)
if "LAB_TOKEN" not in os.environ:
    sys.stderr.write("missing LAB_TOKEN\n")
    sys.exit(2)
baseUrl = os.environ["LAB_URL"]
tokenVal = os.environ["LAB_TOKEN"]
baseUrl = baseUrl.rstrip("/")
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + tokenVal}
try:
    respRealm = requests.get(baseUrl + "/api/kc/realm", headers=headers)
except Exception as ex:
    sys.stderr.write("request failed for realm api: " + str(ex) + "\n")
    sys.exit(2)
if respRealm.status_code != 200:
    sys.stderr.write("realm api returned status " + str(respRealm.status_code) + "\n")
    sys.exit(2)
try:
    respEvidence = requests.get(baseUrl + "/kc/realm", headers=headers)
except Exception as ex:
    sys.stderr.write("request failed for evidence page: " + str(ex) + "\n")
    sys.exit(2)
if respEvidence.status_code != 200:
    sys.stderr.write("evidence page returned status " + str(respEvidence.status_code) + "\n")
    sys.exit(2)
try:
    dataRealm = respRealm.json()
except Exception as ex:
    sys.stderr.write("invalid json for realm: " + str(ex) + "\n")
    sys.exit(2)
if not isinstance(dataRealm, dict):
    sys.stderr.write("unexpected realm data type\n")
    sys.exit(2)
policyVal = dataRealm.get("passwordPolicy")
if policyVal is not None and not isinstance(policyVal, str):
    sys.stderr.write("unexpected passwordPolicy type\n")
    sys.exit(2)
expectedReq = "passwordPolicy contains length(12) or greater and upperCase(1), lowerCase(1), digits(1) and specialChars(1)"
if policyVal is None:
    statusVal = "fail"
    observedVal = None
    detailVal = "Realm password policy is missing and does not satisfy length 12 or greater with upper-case, lower-case, digit and special-character requirements."
else:
    foundPairs = re.findall(r"([A-Za-z]+)\s*\(\s*(\d+)\s*\)", policyVal)
    parsedVals = {}
    for pairName, pairNum in foundPairs:
        parsedVals[pairName] = int(pairNum)
    hasLength = "length" in parsedVals and parsedVals["length"] >= 12
    hasUpper = "upperCase" in parsedVals and parsedVals["upperCase"] >= 1
    hasLower = "lowerCase" in parsedVals and parsedVals["lowerCase"] >= 1
    hasDigits = "digits" in parsedVals and parsedVals["digits"] >= 1
    hasSpecial = "specialChars" in parsedVals and parsedVals["specialChars"] >= 1
    if hasLength and hasUpper and hasLower and hasDigits and hasSpecial:
        statusVal = "pass"
        observedVal = policyVal
        detailVal = "Realm password policy satisfies length 12 or greater with upper-case, lower-case, digit and special-character requirements."
    else:
        statusVal = "fail"
        observedVal = policyVal
        detailVal = "Realm password policy does not satisfy length 12 or greater with upper-case, lower-case, digit and special-character requirements."
print(json.dumps({"status": statusVal, "observed": observedVal, "expected": expectedReq, "detail": detailVal, "evidence_page": "/kc/realm"}))

before.expected: passwordPolicy contains length(12) or greater and upperCase(1), lowerCase(1), digits(1) and specialChars(1)
before.detail: Realm password policy does not satisfy length 12 or greater with upper-case, lower-case, digit and special-character requirements.

inspection.comment: The screenshot shows passwordPolicy as length(8), which lacks the required length 12 and complexity items.

control.title: Account lockout after repeated login failures
control.objective: Account lockout on repeated login failures is enabled and triggers after at most 5 failures.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve GET /api/kc/realm and verify bruteForceProtected is true and failureFactor is less than or equal to 5.
control.risk: Without lockout, attackers can perform unlimited online password-guessing attacks against all accounts.
control.recommendation: Enable brute-force protection in the realm and set the failure threshold to 5 or fewer attempts.
control.cause: Brute-force protection was likely never enabled or was configured with a permissive threshold.

before.detail: Checked 1 realm; bruteForceProtected is false and failureFactor is 30.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows bruteForceProtected is False and failureFactor is 30, matching the automated failure.

control.title: Idle session timeout limited to 15 minutes
control.objective: Idle SSO sessions expire after at most 15 minutes and idle timeout is not disabled.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve GET /api/kc/realm and verify ssoSessionIdleTimeout is set to 900 seconds or less.
control.expected: ssoSessionIdleTimeout<=900 (seconds) and not disabled or zero
control.risk: Overly long idle sessions allow session hijacking and unauthorized use of unattended workstations.
control.recommendation: Set the realm idle session timeout to 900 seconds or less.
control.cause: The realm session timeout was likely left at the Keycloak default value exceeding 15 minutes.

before.expected: ssoSessionIdleTimeout<=900 (seconds) and not disabled or zero
before.detail: Realm ssoSessionIdleTimeout is 28800 seconds, exceeding the 900-second limit.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows ssoSessionIdleTimeout is 28800 seconds, exceeding the 900-second limit.

control.title: Logging of administration actions
control.objective: All administration actions are recorded as admin events in the realm.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve GET /api/kc/realm and verify adminEventsEnabled is true.
control.risk: Without admin audit logging, malicious or erroneous privileged changes cannot be detected, investigated or attributed.
control.recommendation: Enable admin events recording in the realm and retain the logs in the central SIEM.
control.cause: Admin event logging was likely never enabled during realm hardening.

before.detail: Realm representation reports adminEventsEnabled=false, so administration actions are not recorded.

inspection.comment: The screenshot shows adminEventsEnabled as False, matching the automated test failure.

control.title: No generic or shared administrator accounts
control.objective: No holder of the realm role admin is a generic or shared account, with each admin having a nominative username of form initiale.nom and a personal email.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve all members of the realm role admin via paginated GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users and verify username and email are nominative and not function or shared-mailbox values.
control.expected: username matches initiale.nom pattern and email is personal (not ops, admin, root or ops-partage@, admin@) for every object from GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users
control.risk: Shared privileged accounts destroy accountability and allow uncontrolled, non-attributable administrator access.
control.recommendation: Remove admin rights from all generic or shared accounts and replace them with nominative accounts.
control.cause: Operational convenience likely led to creation of function accounts with admin rights without enforcing nominative provisioning.

before.expected: username matches initiale.nom pattern and email is personal (not ops, admin, root or ops-partage@, admin@) for every object from GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users
before.detail: Checked 7 admin users, found 1 with generic or non-nominative username or email.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows seven admin accounts including generic account support-n2 with non-nominative username and email.
